### God's Concern for the Nations
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/gods-concern-nations
Passage: Genesis 10:32
Points:
- God's redemptive plan encompasses not only Israel but all the peoples and nations of the earth.
- The Table of Nations shows the fulfillment of God's post-flood command to multiply and fill the earth.
- The seventy representative nations symbolize the fullness of humanity descended from Noah.
- Situating ancient Israel in the midst of these nations was an implicit summons to be a light to the world.
- Christians are called to reflect God's heart for all peoples through intentional world evangelization.

### In Praise of Genesis 10
Author: Meredith van der Klip
Site: The Gospel Coalition Australia
URL: https://au.thegospelcoalition.org/article/in-praise-of-genesis-10/
Passage: Genesis 10:6-14
Points:
- Bible readers often skip genealogies, but Genesis 10 contains vital context for understanding Scripture.
- The lineage of Ham introduces major biblical adversaries of Israel, including Egypt, Canaan, and the Philistines.
- Cush’s son Nimrod established kingdoms in Babylon and Assyria, the future conquerors and exilers of God’s people.
- Tracking these family lines equips readers to understand conflicts that unfold throughout the Old and New Testaments.
- Christians are encouraged to press into difficult genealogies rather than abandoning their annual Bible reading plans.

### Bible Pathways - Jan. 4, 2009
Author: Bible Pathways Ministries
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathways-jan-4-2009-11597646.html
Passage: Genesis 10:8
Points:
- Nimrod exemplifies humanity's fallen craving for prestige, earthly dominance, and self-rule.
- Building kingdoms in human pride stands in direct defiance of God's Word and kingdom.
- Lasting human unity cannot be achieved through worldly monuments, but only spiritually through Jesus Christ.
- Believers must resist cultural self-promotion and keep their hearts set on the eternal kingdom of God.
